newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JUNE 11.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Parliament yesterday expressed its confidence in the cabinet. The entire coalition (100 votes) and the chairman of the budgetary committee Jozef Wagner voted for the cabinet. Wagner's was the deciding vote, and it was conditioned by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus' promise to present a concept for privatising state stakes in banks.

- After the parliament meeting yesterday, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus announced that the second set of budget cuts this year will amount to 16.5 billion crowns. Although yesterday the total mentioned was 20 billion, the extra 3.5 billion will be saved through changes in social laws.

- The general director of Unipetrol, which owns Ceska Rafinerska, said selling state-owned Benzina and a 30 percent stake in Cepro a.s. to foreigners would probably threaten further development for Ceska Rafinerska.

- The three Czech manufactures of seamless iron pipes decided to fight the current antidumping surcharge from the EU against their products. The Industry and Trade Ministry will meet with the EU on Friday in Brussels.
- An 83 percent stake in the lock company FAB a.s. went to the Swedish lock-making company Assa Abloy.
- According to the economic-business director of Chemopetrol Litvinov, if all negative predictions for the crown are fulfilled, it could cause Chemopetrol to lose 350 million crowns of its profits.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Ford automotive corporation decided to invest another few tens of millions of dollars into expanding its factory Autopal Novy Jicin, which manufactures lighting technology for automobiles.

- A leading world cigarette manufacturer, British-American Tobacco, which controls three percent of the Czech market due to Lucky Strike and HB cigarettes, will apparently close its only domestic factory in Marianske Lazne.
- From Thursday, Investicni a Postovni Banka will increase its fixed yearly interest rates on certain accounts of up to one month.
- The fund AG 21 administered by InvestAge obtained a one-third stake in Apollon Holding from Agrobanka, C.S. Holding, A-Leasing and the Cypress bank Daehe.

- The development plans of small and medium sized companies operating domestically should be supported by a new risk-capital fund, which should obtain at least one billion crowns from investors including CSOB, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and Dutch ING Bank.
LIDOVE NOVINY - The new chairman of the representative club of the Civic Democratic Party as of yesterday is Parliament Vice-chairman Jiri Honajzer.

- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus met with French Justice Minister Elisabeth Guigou, who conveyed greetings from new French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin. Both politicians assured the interest of both sides in contiuing fruitful cooperation.

- Direct French investment into the Czech Republic last year amounted to $547 million, which is 7.8 percent of all foreign investment in the Czech Republic and fifth among other countries. Czech-French trade amounted to $1.8 billion, exports were $626 million and imports $1.2 billion.

- The fifth annual economic forum of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe begins today in Prague. Delegates from the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development, the WTO, the International Labour Organisation, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the European Investment Bank, the IMF and the European Council should participate.
PRAVO - The Czech National Bank issued a foreign exchange licence to Moravia Banka, enabling it to extend its services into international banking.

- According to the vice-chairman of the Czech Statistical Bureau, Ivan Sujan, the cabinet should have waited at least one month to decide on budget cuts, due to positive April results from industrial and construction output.
